evidenceAudit.scope: Women planning or capable of pregnancy: folic acid, review of medical conditions and medicines, and diabetes-specific preconception care. Verified against the Saudi Public Health Authority Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (folic acid), NICE NG3 (preconception care in diabetes) and the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

pathophysiology.summary: Organogenesis happens in the first weeks after conception, often before pregnancy is recognised. Neural-tube closure needs adequate folate; poorly controlled diabetes and some medicines (e.g. ACE inhibitors, statins) harm the embryo — so risks must be addressed before conception.
keyMechanisms: Folate deficiency increases neural-tube defect risk; supplementation before conception reduces it.
Hyperglycaemia around conception raises the risk of congenital anomalies and miscarriage — the basis for preconception HbA1c targets (NICE NG3).
Teratogenic or fetotoxic medicines (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, statins, some anti-epileptics) should be reviewed before stopping contraception.

symptoms: Plans for pregnancy; contraception; previous pregnancy outcomes.
Chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy, thyroid disease); current medicines.
physicalSigns: Signs of diabetes complications (retinopathy, nephropathy) in women with diabetes.
redFlags: Diabetes with high HbA1c — advise contraception until control improves (NICE NG3)
Teratogenic medicines in a woman stopping contraception

clinicalManagement.title: Folic acid
actions: All women planning or capable of pregnancy: folic acid 0.4–0.8 mg daily from at least 1 month before conception through the first 2–3 months (Saudi PHA 2023).
High risk of neural-tube defects (epilepsy, diabetes, previous NTD baby): 4 mg daily (Saudi PHA) — NICE NG3 advises 5 mg daily until 12 weeks for women with diabetes.

clinicalManagement.title: Diabetes
actions: Explain benefits of good preconception control; agree HbA1c targets; measure up to monthly (NICE NG3).
Stop oral glucose-lowering agents except metformin and switch to insulin; stop statins before pregnancy (NICE NG3).
Retinal and renal assessment as above.

clinicalManagement.title: General review
actions: Review medicines for pregnancy safety; advise on weight, smoking and alcohol (NICE NG201 early-pregnancy information).

learningObjectives: Reduce preventable pregnancy risks through preconception folic acid and medical review.

keyPoints: Folic acid 0.4–0.8 mg from 1 month before conception.
High risk: 4 mg (PHA) or 5 mg (NICE, diabetes).
Diabetes: optimise HbA1c, switch to insulin ± metformin, stop statins.
Review teratogenic medicines before stopping contraception.
pitfalls: Starting folic acid only after a positive test.
Continuing ACE inhibitors or statins when planning pregnancy.
Rapid glucose lowering before retinal assessment.

patientEducation: Plan pregnancy; continue contraception until ready.
Healthy weight, stop smoking, avoid alcohol.
lifestyleAndDiet: Healthy diet and activity; weight optimisation before pregnancy.
mdtReferrals: Nephrology if diabetic kidney disease (NICE NG3).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review before stopping contraception; women with diabetes are seen in a preconception diabetes clinic (NICE NG3).
